bull.b: Affirm has developed substantial operating and free cash flow while materially reducing leverage, improving its ability to fund growth and absorb credit or funding volatility. Stronger capitalization also reduces dependence on external financing and provides greater flexibility for product investment and strategic expansion.

Growth across Pay-in-X and Affirm Card indicates increasing engagement beyond the core checkout use case, while dynamic underwriting supports controlled expansion. The combination of product adoption and credit discipline can strengthen customer relationships and preserve unit economics as volumes scale.

The Sam’s Club collaboration adds a large retail distribution channel and extends Affirm’s reach from online checkout toward physical locations. A multi-year relationship can support transaction growth, merchant visibility, and broader consumer adoption if the planned rollout executes successfully.

bear.b: The sharp latest-period revenue decline creates uncertainty about the durability and mix of growth, even though profitability improved substantially. Inconsistent gross-profit and EBIT margin reporting further reduces confidence in how repeatable the reported earnings improvement will be over coming periods.

Physical-retail expansion remains operationally demanding because connectivity, point-of-sale integration, and checkout failure handling require further improvement. These frictions can delay offline volume growth, increase implementation effort, and make the planned expansion less immediate than online distribution gains.

Affirm still has meaningful room to expand merchant coverage, but the low current penetration also shows that distribution growth depends on closing lengthy enterprise integrations. Multi-quarter sales cycles can slow transaction-volume scaling and leave near-term results reliant on existing merchant relationships.
